cases.title: Weather integration is real, and any fallback is explicitly labelled
cases.requirement: The system must fetch weather from a real provider. If no provider can be reached it must fall back to a clearly labelled offline climatology estimate with is_simulated=true, and must never present a fabricated value as if it came from an API.
cases.notes: The provider chain is OpenWeatherMap -> Open-Meteo -> offline-climatology. Open-Meteo needs no key, so the common case is genuinely live. The offline branch is the only place simulated numbers exist and it is labelled everywhere it surfaces (bundle, snapshot row, UI banner, PDF).
expected: The response states which provider was used ('source' + 'provider').
A live provider (open-meteo / openweathermap) implies is_simulated=false.
An offline fallback implies is_simulated=true AND source='offline-climatology'.
The provider and the simulated flag agree with each other - no unlabelled fabrication.
A 7-day daily forecast is returned with ET0 and rainfall totals.

cases.title: Crop suitability scored per factor with retrieved citations
cases.requirement: The crop planning agent must return a defensible suitability verdict that decomposes into weighted factors, states what data was missing, and cites the reference documents it retrieved.
cases.notes: Retrieval is a real FAISS IndexFlatIP search over 23 agricultural reference documents; the scores shown here are cosine similarities of the query against the retrieved chunks.
expected: A suitability score and a status verdict are returned.
Every factor carries a verdict, a weight, a measured value and the required range.
Weights sum to 1.0 so the score is reproducible from the factors.
The document catalogue lists crops with their agronomic requirement bands.
At least one citation from the FAISS knowledge base is attached to the assessment.
Missing inputs are declared rather than silently imputed.

cases.title: Irrigation is a proposal gated behind human authorisation
cases.requirement: The irrigation agent must never trigger physical irrigation. It must produce a recommendation flagged as requiring human authorisation, raise an approval request, and only schedule the activity once a named reviewer decides.
cases.notes: Approval authorises the recorded plan only. There is no irrigation-hardware adapter in the codebase: the deepest effect of a decision is FarmActivity.status changing from 'planned' to 'scheduled'.

decision_body.decision_note: Reviewed on site; soil moisture probe checked against a hand check.

The safety contract states explicitly that approval authorises documentation, not hardware.
After a named reviewer approves, the irrigation activity becomes 'scheduled'.

cases.title: Crop risk is reported as favourable environment and cross-checked by a trained model
cases.requirement: Risk findings must be phrased as 'Environmental conditions favourable for X'. The system must never claim a disease is confirmed, must declare its non-diagnostic disclaimer, and must agree with the trained ML severity model.
cases.notes: Risk statements describe the environment only. Confirming a disease needs field scouting or a laboratory test, which is exactly what recommended_investigation tells the reader to do.
expected: Findings are phrased 'Environmental conditions favourable for ...'.
No finding contains a confirmation or diagnosis phrase.
Every persisted finding carries is_diagnosis=false.
A non-diagnostic disclaimer is returned alongside the findings.
The trained risk classifier agrees with the rule-based severity, or the disagreement is reported.
Each finding cites the evidence it was derived from.
